name: The freight shed on the south bank below the Dearborn draw

documented_range.note: NO SOURCE RECORD IN THIS REPOSITORY DATES THIS BUILDING, BECAUSE NO SOURCE RECORD NAMES IT. The range is the reconstruction's own bracket and it is graded as one. It is the SAME bracket the four north-bank sheds of T-0133 carry, deliberately: it opens on 1834-08-01, the date `dearborn_street_drawbridge` opens on, because the reason to stand a freight shed on this reach is that the crossing brought the town's traffic to it, and it closes at the end of 1835 because nothing follows the building and a range that ran on would be claiming survival nobody attested. What IS held is the treatment, not the date: image 3 of the owner's brief of 2026-08-18 (data/sources/assets/owner_brief_2026_08_18/README.md) is an engraving of this reach from farther out, and it draws low warehouses on BOTH banks below the bridge. A tier-5 retrospective plate can attest that the banks below the draw carried working sheds; it cannot date one.

change_note: One phase. This building is a reconstruction of a TYPE the plate puts on this bank, not a record of a building anybody named, so it has no history to divide into phases and inventing one would be inventing twice.

placement.position_note:
INVENTED, AND PLACED BY A RULE RATHER THAN BY A PLATE. The plate that puts sheds on this bank is image 3 of the owner's brief of 2026-08-18 (data/sources/assets/owner_brief_2026_08_18/README.md): masts crowd the reach below the bridge, a light structure near the mouth, LOW WAREHOUSES ON THE BANKS. It is a TIER-5 PICTORIAL source — retrospective, drawn decades after 1835 — and this project's standing rule for one is that it may drive massing, form, materials and setting and may NEVER drive a coordinate. So the plate decides that a shed stands on this bank and nothing else about where.

WHY THIS BANK CARRIES A SHED ONLY NOW, AND IT IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT A CHANGE OF MIND. T-0134 measured the whole reach — dearborn_street_drawbridge (local E 699.2) east to the Reservation's west line (E 842.0) — and found NOT ONE position, at any bearing, where the smallest footprint family F1 allows would stand on dry ground outside a platted corridor with less than 0.35 m of relief. The south bank was refused on that reading and the refusal is recorded in data/exclusions.json as `south_bank_warehouses_dearborn_reach`. T-1629 then re-traced the town slough's mouth to Wright's own re-entrant east of State Street and FILLED the mouth this project had cut west of it, and the ground that had been the old channel and its approach cuts came up about a metre above the water and dead flat. T-1636 re-read the reach on that ground: 91 positions appeared at 0.30 m of relief where there had been none, 81 of them standing in the fort road's own travelled way, and TEN clear of it. This is one of the ten. `tools/measure_south_bank_ground.py` is the reading and `tools/south_bank_ground_baseline.json` is what it is held to.

WHERE IS DERIVED, from three committed things and one stated setback. (1) THE EASTING is the westernmost station between South Water Street's platted corridor and State Street's at which the whole rectangle stands on free ground: at local E 806.5 it does, and 0.5 m west of that its west corner enters South Water's corridor. It is not chosen for the view, it is the first ground east of the platted town. (2) THE NORTHING AND THE BEARING come off the fort road, data/streets/1835.json, `track_width_m` 5.5: at E 806.5 its drawn centreline stands at N 4.164, so the north edge of its travelled way is 2.75 m north of that, and the front wall is set 1.25 m back from that edge and squared to the road's own bearing at that station (6.226 degrees). Measured over the whole footprint the nearest point of the building stands 3.98 m from the centreline, which is 1.23 m of clear ground between its wall and the wheel line. (3) THE COMMITTED HEIGHTFIELD, data/terrain/epochs/e1834_harbor_cut: sampled on the same half-metre lattice the reading uses, 252 points, the ground under this footprint stands between 1.027 m and 1.300 m above the water surface — 0.273 m of relief across the whole rectangle, inside the 0.30 m `generate_block_infill.MAX_RELIEF_M` allows — so the walls share one walker surface without a cut or a fill.

WHY THE SETBACK IS 1.25 m AND NOT THE 2.00 m THE NORTH BANK KEEPS. On the north bank the sheds stand back 2.00 m from North Water Street's travelled edge onto an open plateau. Here the window is 9.5 m wide — South Water's corridor ends at E 805.0 and State Street's begins at E 814.5 — and the flat terrace runs out at about N 16 where the bank falls to the water at N 24.5 to 26.0. At a 2.00 m setback the back wall stands half a metre further down that fall and the rectangle's relief reaches 0.353 m, past the clause. The SETBACK is what gave way rather than the clause, and both figures are stated so the trade is visible.

WHAT IT STANDS INSIDE, SAID PLAINLY: the fort road's own RECONSTRUCTED 12 m corridor, which this building is 1.23 m inside of measured from the travelled way. That corridor is not a legal reservation and cannot be one — `fort_road` carries `geometry_confidence: reconstructed`, nobody traced the road and no source names it — so there is no platted width here for a building to lap. It laps no PLATTED corridor: `tools/measure_corridor_intrusion.py` reads it clear of all 33.

WORKING UNCERTAINTY: total. Nothing states that a building stood at this station on 1835-07-01. What would replace this placement is a lot record on the river side of South Water Street, a forwarding merchant's advertisement giving an address on this reach, or a contemporary view of the south bank. docs/LIBERTIES.md owns the invention.

THE ROAD THIS SHED WAS SQUARED TO IS NO LONGER ON THIS REACH (T-1637, the same day, hours after the seating). The fort road crossed the State slough's new mouth in open water - 3.60 m of its centreline below the surface, no crossing recorded and none evidenced anywhere for a road on the United States Reservation - so its western terminus was moved onto State Street at the toe of the Slough Log Bridge's southern approach, and the reach that ran east past this shed is gone. WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE, stated rather than left for a reader to discover. THIS BUILDING DOES NOT MOVE: its EASTING is the westernmost station between the two platted corridors at which the whole rectangle stands free, its ground is the filled channel's and is untouched, and its committed position now stands 41.2 m from the road's centreline where it stood 13.7 m from it - so the one hazard the road's presence argued about, a building in a travelled way, is further from being true than it was, and no platted corridor is any nearer. WHAT IS NOW UNCHECKABLE, AND IT IS THIS RECORD'S OWN RULE: the NORTHING, the BEARING and the wagon door's side were read off the fort road's drawn travelled way - 1.25 m of setback from its north edge, squared to its bearing here, the door to the road. Those three numbers stand where they were written and the road they were read off does not. They were invented when they were written and they are invented now, at the same `reconstructed` grade; what has been lost is the ability to re-derive them by hand from a committed line, which is exactly what the derivation block below says this placement always depended on. NOTHING IS RE-SEATED HERE TO HIDE THAT: re-facing or re-seating this shed is a change of geometry and a re-bake, and it is filed as its own question rather than smuggled into the run that moved the road. The relief test is independent of the road and still holds: the 252-point lattice under the footprint stands 1.027 to 1.300 m above the water surface, 0.273 m of relief, inside the generators' 0.30 m.
placement.symbolic_location: On the south bank of the main stem below the Dearborn Street drawbridge, on the last town ground east of South Water Street's platted corridor and west of State Street's, standing between the fort road and the river with its wagon door to the road.

footprint.note: INVENTED AT THE SMALLEST SIZE THE PROGRAMME'S BAND FOR THE FAMILY ALLOWS, because it is the only size this ground takes. 5.4864 x 9.7536 m is 18 x 32 ft, the floor of family F1 (freight or storage shed) in data/reconstruction/1835_building_inventory.json, whose band runs to 28 x 50 ft. It is also the exact rectangle `tools/measure_south_bank_ground.py` sweeps the reach with, so the building and the reading that admitted it are the same size and the placement can be checked against the reading that found it. The frontage is the short side and the depth runs back from the road, which is the crosswalk's own description of F1 — a long building with wide doors — and what the plate's low sheds read as. The long axis cannot run along the road instead: 9.7536 m of frontage does not fit between South Water Street's platted corridor and State Street's, which are 9.5 m apart on this bank. No source gives this building a dimension because no source gives this building.

construction.note: The crosswalk's F1 entry gives 'vertical-board frame' for a freight shed, which is the archetype's `plank`: sawn boards nailed up vertically with the gaps showing. The same treatment the four north-bank sheds of T-0133 carry, because the plate draws the two banks' buildings alike. Invented either way — nothing states how any building on this bank was built.

wall_height_m.note: The crosswalk's F1 eave band is 10-13 ft (3.05-3.96 m) and this is 11.2 ft, inside it and a little lower than the north bank's 3.6 m. A cart and a stacked load set the floor; the plate's word for these buildings is LOW and that sets the ceiling, and the smallest footprint in the family carries the lowest eave in it rather than the same one a building half again its size carries. Invented.

roof_type.note: F1's roof line in the crosswalk is 'gable or shed'. Gable, which is the near-universal roof of a frame building of this type and date, and the roof the north-bank row carries. Invented.

roof_pitch_deg.note: F1's pitch band is 5:12 to 9:12, which is 22.6 to 36.9 degrees; this is 30.0 degrees, inside it and the same as the north bank's. No source gives a pitch for anything on this bank. Invented.

door.note: A freight shed is a building goods go into and out of by cart, so the opening is the archetype's `wagon` door rather than a man door — which is also what the crosswalk's F1 entry means by 'wide doors; low openings'. The only way a cart reaches this ground is the fort road, so the door is on that side. Invented, like the building.

door_side.note: The door faces the fort road, which is the side the traffic is on and the only side a cart can come from — the river is behind the building and the two platted corridors are at either end. The archetype's front faces north at rotation 0 and this record is rotated to face the road, so `front` here is the road side and the back wall is the river side. Invented.

paint.note: Unpainted boards, which is the archetype's own default and the treatment image 3 and image 11 both show on working river buildings. Paint on a freight shed would be the larger claim. Invented.

function.note: The use comes from the plate and from the place. Image 3 of the owner's brief of 2026-08-18 draws low warehouses on the banks of the reach below the drawbridge, and this reach is where the river traffic, the town's only crossing of the main stem and the road to the fort all met in July 1835. The specific goods, the trade and the operator are not inferred and are not recorded: an occupant would be a person, and this record claims a building.

research_note: A RECONSTRUCTED BUILDING, AND THE SECOND HALF OF T-0134 — the half that finding said it could not take. T-0133 built the four north-bank sheds image 3 of the owner's brief draws and left this bank empty, with one sentence in all four of their records: the platted South Water Street corridor reaches to within about 1.7 m of the traced 1834 waterline at the Dearborn reach, so there is no ground there for a building that is not standing in the platted street. T-0134 turned that spot reading into a command over the whole reach and the refusal held, harder: not one position at any bearing, at 0.30 m of relief or at 0.35 m. THAT SENTENCE IS STILL TRUE OF THE FRONTAGE THE PLATE DRAWS, and this building does not stand on it. Beside the platted street — west of South Water's own east end at local E 805.0 — the reading is still zero at every relief clause it is reported at, and one clause HARDER than when the refusal was written: the three positions that used to stand there at a metre of relief are gone. What changed is east of the street's end. T-1629 re-traced the town slough to Wright's own re-entrant east of State Street and filled the mouth this project had cut west of it; the old channel and its approach cuts came up flat and dry, and T-1636 re-read the reach. Ten positions clear of the fort road's travelled way, at 0.30 m of relief, on ground that had been a channel of this project's own making. This is the westernmost of them. WHAT IS HELD: image 3 of the brief (data/sources/assets/owner_brief_2026_08_18/README.md), an engraving of the reach below the Dearborn drawbridge showing low warehouses on BOTH banks; and image 11, the retrospective painting of South Water Street in 1834, which shows what a working river frontage in this town looked like. Both are tier-5 pictorial and neither is yet held as a source record — T-0075 owns that — so this record cites committed paths rather than a source_id, and no source is claimed. WHAT IS CONJECTURAL: the building, its station, its size, its construction, its roof, its opening and its date. All of it, as on the north bank. WHAT WOULD UPGRADE IT: a lot record on the river side of South Water Street, a forwarding merchant's advertisement giving an address on this reach, or a contemporary view of the south bank. Built under the owner's standing ruling of 2026-08-18 — 'you are totally fine to be liberal with adding reconstructed items when i ask for things, you can just label and mark them as such'.
